triggerOn.documentation: The status codes and errors from the route's target that cause the gateway to send the request to the first fallback target. If you omit triggerOn, the gateway falls back on 5XX status codes and on the CONNECTION_ERROR, FIRST_BYTE_TIMEOUT, and UNROUTABLE errors. If you specify triggerOn, only the status codes and errors that you list trigger a fallback.

firstByteTimeoutMilliseconds.documentation: The maximum time, in milliseconds, from sending the request to the route's target until the first byte of the response body arrives. If the time expires, the gateway abandons the request and treats it as a FIRST_BYTE_TIMEOUT error. If you don't specify a value, no timeout is enforced.

circuitBreaker.documentation: Specifies whether the gateway temporarily stops sending your requests to a failing target. The circuit breaker tracks each combination of target and model separately. With the circuit breaker enabled, the gateway skips one or more targets and models that fail repeatedly, and your requests go to the next target in the chain. The gateway always tries the last remaining target in the chain. The gateway enables the circuit breaker by default.

targetFallback.documentation: The ordered list of fallback targets. The gateway tries each target in order until a response doesn't match that target's triggers, and returns that response to the caller. If every target fails, the gateway returns the last response. You can specify up to two fallback targets. Each combination of target and model, including the route's target, can appear only once.

Fallback.documentation: The fallback configuration for a route to an inference target. Defines an ordered list of fallback targets to try when a request to the route's target fails, and the conditions that trigger a fallback. A fallback can occur only before the gateway sends the first byte of the response to the caller. After a streaming response starts, the gateway doesn't fall back.

targetName.documentation: The name of the gateway target to fall back to. The target must be an inference target.

model.documentation: The model ID to send to this fallback target. If you don't specify a model, the gateway sends the model from the original request.

triggerOn.documentation: The status codes and errors from this target that cause the gateway to send the request to the next fallback target. This setting isn't inherited from the route. If you omit it, the gateway uses the default triggers: 5XX status codes and the CONNECTION_ERROR, FIRST_BYTE_TIMEOUT, and UNROUTABLE errors.

firstByteTimeoutMilliseconds.documentation: The maximum time, in milliseconds, from sending the request to this target until the first byte of the response body arrives. This setting isn't inherited from the route. If you don't specify a value, no timeout is enforced.

FallbackTarget.documentation: Specifies a target to send the request to when the previous target in the fallback chain fails. Includes the target name, the model to send, and the conditions that trigger a fallback from this target to the next one.

statusCodes.documentation:
The HTTP status codes returned by the target that trigger a fallback. You can specify the following:

  • An exact status code – A three-digit code, such as 429.

  • A class of status codes – The first digit followed by XX, such as 5XX, which matches every code from 500 to 599.

Only 4XX and 5XX codes are supported. Throttling by the gateway itself doesn't trigger a fallback.

errors.documentation:
The errors that trigger a fallback. You can specify the following:

  • CONNECTION_ERROR – The gateway couldn't connect to the target because the connection was refused, reset, or timed out. The request didn't reach the target.

  • FIRST_BYTE_TIMEOUT – The target accepted the connection but didn't return the first byte of the response within firstByteTimeoutMilliseconds. The gateway abandons the request before any of the response reaches you.

  • UNROUTABLE – The gateway couldn't route the request to the target, for example because the target doesn't exist or doesn't support the request path. These errors don't count toward the circuit breaker.

FallbackTriggers.documentation: The conditions that trigger a fallback to the next target. A fallback occurs if the response matches any of the specified status codes or errors.

description.documentation: A human-readable description of the finding. This provides detailed information about the issue, recommendation, or validation result to help users understand and address the finding.

Finding.documentation: Represents a finding or issue discovered during policy generation or validation. Findings provide insights about potential problems, recommendations, or validation results from policy analysis operations. Finding types include: VALID (policy is ready to use), INVALID (policy has validation errors that must be fixed), NOT_TRANSLATABLE (input couldn't be converted to policy), ALLOW_ALL (policy would allow all actions, potential security risk), ALLOW_NONE (policy would allow no actions, unusable), DENY_ALL (policy would deny all actions, may be too restrictive), and DENY_NONE (policy would deny no actions, ineffective). Review all findings before creating policies from generated assets to ensure they match your security requirements.

mode.documentation:
The enforcement mode for the policy engine. Valid values include:

  • LOG_ONLY - The policy engine evaluates each action against your policies and adds traces on whether tool calls would be allowed or denied, but does not enforce the decision. Use this mode to test and validate policies before enabling enforcement.

  • ENFORCE - The policy engine evaluates actions against your policies and enforces decisions by allowing or denying agent operations. Test and validate policies in LOG_ONLY mode before enabling enforcement to avoid unintended denials or adversely affecting production traffic.

GatewayPolicyEngineConfiguration.documentation: The configuration for a policy engine associated with a gateway. A policy engine is a collection of policies that evaluates and authorizes agent tool calls. When associated with a gateway, the policy engine intercepts all agent requests and determines whether to allow or deny each action based on the defined policies.

sources.documentation: The resources served by the consent portal.

consentPortalArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the consent portal.

consentPortalId.documentation: The unique identifier of the consent portal.

createdAt.documentation: The timestamp for when the consent portal was created.

executionRoleArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that the consent portal assumes to access the resources defined in its sources.

idpConfig.documentation: The identity provider configuration that the consent portal uses to authenticate end users.

name.documentation: The name of the consent portal.

portalUrl.documentation: The URL used to access the consent portal.

status.documentation: The current status of the consent portal.

statusReason.documentation: A message that provides additional information about the current status of the consent portal.

updatedAt.documentation: The timestamp for when the consent portal was last updated.

datasetId.documentation: The unique identifier of the dataset to retrieve.

datasetVersion.documentation: Version to retrieve: "DRAFT" or a version number. Defaults to DRAFT if absent.

datasetArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the dataset.

datasetId.documentation: The unique identifier of the dataset.

datasetVersion.documentation: The resolved version: "DRAFT" (default) or the requested version number.

status.documentation: The current status of the dataset.

draftStatus.documentation: Publish synchronization state. Only authoritative when status is ACTIVE. MODIFIED indicates DRAFT has unpublished changes. UNMODIFIED indicates DRAFT matches the latest published version.

failureReason.documentation: Populated when status is CREATE_FAILED, UPDATE_FAILED, or DELETE_FAILED. Describes the reason for the failure.

schemaType.documentation: The schema type declared at create time. Immutable after creation.

kmsKeyArn.documentation: KMS key ARN used for server-side encryption on service Amazon S3 writes, if configured.

exampleCount.documentation: The number of examples in the DRAFT.

downloadUrl.documentation: Presigned Amazon S3 URL to download the consolidated dataset file for the resolved version. Expires after 5 minutes. Omitted if the file does not yet exist.

downloadUrlExpiresAt.documentation: Expiry timestamp for the download URL.

createdAt.documentation: The timestamp when the dataset was created.

updatedAt.documentation: The timestamp when the dataset was last updated.

tags.documentation: The tags associated with the dataset.

evaluatorId.documentation: The unique identifier of the evaluator to retrieve. Can be a built-in evaluator ID (e.g., Builtin.Helpfulness) or a custom evaluator ID.

includedData.documentation: Controls which data is returned in the response. ALL_DATA (default) returns the full evaluator including decrypted instructions and rating scale. For evaluators encrypted with a customer managed KMS key, this requires kms:Decrypt permission on the key. METADATA_ONLY returns evaluator metadata and model configuration without instructions or rating scale, and does not require any KMS permissions.

evaluatorArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the evaluator.

evaluatorId.documentation: The unique identifier of the evaluator.

evaluatorConfig.documentation: The configuration of the evaluator, including LLM-as-a-Judge or code-based settings.

evaluatorType.documentation:
The kind of evaluator resource. Valid values:

  • Builtin – An Amazon Web Services-managed global evaluator.

  • ThirdParty – An Amazon Web Services-managed global evaluator from a third-party provider.

  • Custom – A customer-created evaluator.

  • CustomCode – A customer-created code-based evaluator.

  • CustomDerived – A customer-created evaluator derived from an existing base evaluator.

provider.documentation: The source of the evaluator's logic: Amazon Web Services, a third-party library, or you.

level.documentation: The evaluation level (TOOL_CALL, TRACE, or SESSION) that determines the scope of evaluation.

status.documentation: The current status of the evaluator.

createdAt.documentation: The timestamp when the evaluator was created.

updatedAt.documentation: The timestamp when the evaluator was last updated.

lockedForModification.documentation: Whether the evaluator is locked for modification due to being referenced by active online evaluation configurations.

kmsKeyArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the customer managed KMS key used to encrypt the evaluator's sensitive data. This field is only present for evaluators encrypted with a customer managed key.

rateLimitId.documentation: The unique identifier of the rate limit to retrieve.
The unique identifier of the rate limit.

description.documentation: The human-readable description of the rate limit.

dimensionKeys.documentation: The ordered list of dimension key names that define the scope of this rate limit.

entries.documentation: The list of rule entries that map dimension values to rate configurations.

status.documentation: The current status of the rate limit.

createdAt.documentation: The timestamp when the rate limit was created.

updatedAt.documentation: The timestamp when the rate limit was last updated.

gatewayIdentifier.documentation: The identifier of the gateway to retrieve.

gatewayArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the gateway.

createdAt.documentation: The timestamp when the gateway was created.

updatedAt.documentation: The timestamp when the gateway was last updated.

status.documentation: The current status of the gateway.

statusReasons.documentation: The reasons for the current status of the gateway.

name.documentation: The name of the gateway.

roleArn.documentation: The IAM role ARN that provides permissions for the gateway.

kmsKeyArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the KMS key used to encrypt the gateway.

customTransformConfiguration.documentation: The custom transformation configuration for the gateway. This configuration defines how the gateway transforms requests and responses.

policyEngineConfiguration.documentation: The policy engine configuration for the gateway.

workloadIdentityDetails.documentation: The workload identity details for the gateway.

exceptionLevel.documentation:
The level of detail in error messages returned when invoking the gateway.

  • If the value is DEBUG, granular exception messages are returned to help a user debug the gateway.

  • If the value is omitted, a generic error message is returned to the end user.

webAclArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Amazon Web Services WAF web ACL associated with the gateway.

wafConfiguration.documentation: The Amazon Web Services WAF configuration for the gateway.

gatewayIdentifier.documentation: The identifier of the gateway containing the rule.

ruleId.documentation: The unique identifier of the rule to retrieve.
The unique identifier of the gateway rule.

gatewayArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the gateway that the rule belongs to.

priority.documentation: The priority of the rule. Rules are evaluated in order of priority, with lower numbers evaluated first.

conditions.documentation: The conditions that must be met for the rule to apply.

actions.documentation: The actions to take when the rule conditions are met.

createdAt.documentation: The timestamp when the rule was created.

status.documentation: The current status of the rule.

system.documentation: System-managed metadata for rules created by automated processes.

updatedAt.documentation: The timestamp when the rule was last updated.

GetGatewayRuleResponse.documentation: Create response excludes updatedAt (redundant on create). Get/Update responses include it via their own output structures.

gatewayIdentifier.documentation: The identifier of the gateway that contains the target.

targetId.documentation: The unique identifier of the target to retrieve.

gatewayArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the gateway.

targetId.documentation: The unique identifier of the gateway target.

createdAt.documentation: The timestamp when the gateway target was created.

updatedAt.documentation: The timestamp when the gateway target was last updated.

status.documentation: The current status of the gateway target.

statusReasons.documentation: The reasons for the current status of the gateway target.

name.documentation: The name of the gateway target.

credentialProviderConfigurations.documentation: The credential provider configurations for the gateway target.

metadataConfiguration.documentation: The metadata configuration for HTTP header and query parameter propagation for the retrieved gateway target.

privateEndpoint.documentation: The private endpoint configuration for the gateway target.

privateEndpointManagedResources.documentation: The managed resources created by the gateway for private endpoint connectivity.

authorizationData.documentation: OAuth2 authorization data for the gateway target. This data is returned when a target is configured with a credential provider with authorization code grant type and requires user federation.

protocolType.documentation: The protocol type of the gateway target.

certificateConfigurations.documentation: The private certificate authority (CA) configurations for the gateway target.

harnessId.documentation: The ID of the harness that the endpoint belongs to.

endpointName.documentation: The name of the endpoint to retrieve.

harnessId.documentation: The ID of the harness to retrieve.

harnessVersion.documentation: Specific version of the harness to retrieve. If omitted, returns the current Harness configuration, including its status.

memoryId.documentation: The unique identifier of the memory to retrieve.

view.documentation: The level of detail to return for the memory.

name.documentation: The name of the OAuth2 credential provider to retrieve.

clientSecretArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the client secret in Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager.

clientSecretJsonKey.documentation: The JSON key used to extract the client secret value from the Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager secret.

clientSecretSource.documentation: The source type of the client secret. Either MANAGED if the secret is managed by the service, or EXTERNAL if managed by the user in Amazon Web Services Secrets Manager.

name.documentation: The name of the OAuth2 credential provider.

credentialProviderVendor.documentation: The vendor of the OAuth2 credential provider.

callbackUrl.documentation: Callback URL to register on the OAuth2 credential provider as an allowed callback URL. This URL is where the OAuth2 authorization server redirects users after they complete the authorization flow.

oauth2ProviderConfigOutput.documentation: The configuration output for the OAuth2 provider.

createdTime.documentation: The timestamp when the OAuth2 credential provider was created.

lastUpdatedTime.documentation: The timestamp when the OAuth2 credential provider was last updated.

status.documentation: The current status of the OAuth2 credential provider.

failureReason.documentation: The reason for failure if the OAuth2 credential provider is in a failed state.

onlineEvaluationConfigId.documentation: The unique identifier of the online evaluation configuration to retrieve.

onlineEvaluationConfigArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the online evaluation configuration.

onlineEvaluationConfigId.documentation: The unique identifier of the online evaluation configuration.

onlineEvaluationConfigName.documentation: The name of the online evaluation configuration.

description.documentation: The description of the online evaluation configuration.

rule.documentation: The evaluation rule containing sampling configuration, filters, and session settings.

dataSourceConfig.documentation: The data source configuration specifying CloudWatch log groups and service names to monitor.

evaluators.documentation: The list of evaluators applied during online evaluation.

insights.documentation: The list of insight types configured for this evaluation.

clusteringConfig.documentation: The clustering configuration for periodic batch evaluation.

outputConfig.documentation: The output configuration specifying where evaluation results are written.

evaluationExecutionRoleArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role used for evaluation execution.

status.documentation: The status of the online evaluation configuration.

executionStatus.documentation: The execution status indicating whether the online evaluation is currently running.

createdAt.documentation: The timestamp when the online evaluation configuration was created.

updatedAt.documentation: The timestamp when the online evaluation configuration was last updated.

failureReason.documentation: The reason for failure if the online evaluation configuration execution failed.

paymentManagerId.documentation: The unique identifier of the parent payment manager.

paymentConnectorId.documentation: The unique identifier of the payment connector to retrieve.
